tagline: A long Pacific coast anchored by one of Latin America's largest metros at Lima, with a marquee marine reserve down the coast at Paracas.
summary: Peru pairs the vast Lima metropolitan coast — stacked on the Costa Verde cliffs above a single congested road, with the port of Callao and its wildlife islands offshore — with the Paracas–Ballestas National Reserve ~250km south, one of the continent's signature marine-wildlife trips. Lima's millions move along one coast road while the bay carries only tour and port traffic, and the Ballestas run is served by crowded launches, leaving broad openings for scheduled clean water transport on both poles.
why_marine_mobility: A dense metropolitan coast on a single congested road plus a marquee, launch-served marine reserve give Peru two distinct high-value water cases — essential Lima Bay commuting and premium reserve-and-island leisure — joined by a roadmap coastal express.

demand_signals.label: Lima Costa Verde
demand_signals.note: ~10M-person metro strung along one congested coast road — a classic parallel-water-tier case.

demand_signals.label: Ballestas reserve
demand_signals.note: Peru's marquee marine-wildlife trip at Paracas, reached by crowded launch from El Chaco.

demand_signals.label: Callao islands
demand_signals.note: San Lorenzo and the Palomino sea-lion colony already run boat tours from Callao.

use_cases.title: Bay waterfront run
use_cases.body: A scheduled Lima Bay water link parallels the congested Costa Verde road.

use_cases.title: Reserve express
use_cases.body: A clean foiling run from El Chaco to the Ballestas reserve replaces the crowded launch.

use_cases.title: Island & wildlife hops
use_cases.body: Callao-island and Palomino sea-lion runs on a quiet, low-wake craft.

use_cases.title: Coastal express
use_cases.body: A ~112nm Lima-to-Paracas run down the Pacific, beyond Pioneer range.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Ideal for the sheltered Lima Bay hops and the Paracas reserve run, all inside Pioneer range, where morning-calm Humboldt water and short legs favour a fast, quiet, zero-wake craft.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Required for the ~112nm Lima-Paracas coastal express, beyond Pioneer range — a roadmap corridor for the longer-range hull.

signature_routes: Costa Verde ↔ Callao / La Punta — Lima Bay waterfront run
La Punta ↔ Isla San Lorenzo — sheltered island hop
Paracas (El Chaco) ↔ Ballestas Islands — marine-reserve express
Lima ↔ Paracas — Pacific coastal express (long-range roadmap)
transit_planning: Transport centres on the Lima metro, the Panamericana highway and the Callao port; scheduled passenger water services are undeveloped on both the bay and the Paracas reserve, leaving room for a marine tier.
competitive_landscape: No scheduled fast passenger-vessel network serves the Lima coast or the Paracas reserve; the coast is road-served, the islands and reserve are launch-served — a clean water tier opens new links across both poles with no direct incumbent.
regulatory_note: Maritime matters fall under Peru's DICAPI and the Callao port authority; the Ballestas/Paracas reserve is protected under SERNANP. Passenger-vessel licensing and reserve-access rules frame any scheduled service.
seasonality: The Humboldt current keeps the coast cool and often calm in the morning, with a grey coastal winter (roughly May-October) and strong afternoon Paracas winds in the south; sheltered legs run year-round, exposed legs are day-windowed.

precedents.why_it_matters: Durable premium demand for a marquee marine trip a clean foiling tier can upgrade.
Shows durable leisure demand on Lima Bay a scheduled clean craft can serve.
